title: slo-toolkit: enrich escalation context with SLO links, runbook snippets, and on-call helpers
author: Maya Singh
description:
Motivation: On-call responders often lack quick contextual links when an SLO breach alert fires. This PR enriches the incident-bot's escalation payload with: 1) normalized SLO detail links (target, window, current burn rate), 2) relevant runbook snippets and quick links to playbooks, and 3) lightweight on-call helper functions for priority scoring and suggested actions. The goal is to reduce time-to-remediate by surfacing actionable context in the first notification.

What changed: added a new slo_toolkit context enricher component that queries the SLO catalog, synthesizes short-form summaries, and attaches runbook quicklinks. Hooked the enricher into the incident-bot notification pipeline with configurable opt-in via feature flag. Implemented helper utilities used by the on-call UI to render suggested next steps and escalation links. Added unit and integration tests, updated docs and Helm values for toggle and RBAC.

Checklist:
- [x] slo_toolkit enricher implementation
- [x] incident-bot pipeline integration and feature flag
- [x] unit + integration tests
- [x] docs and runbook examples
- [x] helm chart values and RBAC updates

Notes: the enricher uses the existing SLO catalog API; where the SLO lacks a runbook we fall back to a prioritized list of relevant playbooks. Feature rollout is controlled by RELEASE_FLAG_ENABLE_SLO_ENRICHMENT. Backwards-compatible: if the flag is off or enrichment errors, incident payloads are unchanged (fail-open).

Maya Singh: Added 2s timeout and simple debounce-based batching to reduce SLO API calls; updated tests to simulate timeouts.
Priya Malhotra: Can we surface the exact SLO target in the payload and include the link to the runbook if present? Also suggest a short 'Suggested Actions' list in the message body.
Maya Singh: Included target and runbook_link fields and added suggested_actions array populated from runbook metadata and common responder heuristics.
Jordan Lee: Integration tests flaky on CI due to timing; looks like the test depended on an external catalog. Recommend a mock and faster assertions.
Maya Singh: Replaced external dependency with test-local mock service and increased assertion stability. Rerun CI.
Priya Malhotra: Approving after minor nits addressed in the last commit. Good to ship behind feature flag.
